subject: Dedicated pool concordance: regional surge mapping & operational checkpoints
messages:
From: Rajiv Suresh <rajiv@helionlabs.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marta Alvarez <marta@helionlabs.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Helion — Dedicated pool: region & surge questions

Sean / Monica,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our execs want two quick things before procurement: (1) recommended primary region for launch (we're EU-first but have dev traffic in us-west), and (2) a clear autoscale / burst policy that guarantees no more than 2s median token latency for the first 60s of a traffic spike.

A few constraints from our side:
- GDPR + Dutch data residency preferences for EU customers (primary).
- We expect a warm steady-state of ~180 concurrent sessions, and short warm spikes up to ~1,400 concurrent sessions for product demos.
- We run quantized LLMs (8-bit) in production; we can accept smaller-variant fallbacks if needed.

Can you share an operational checklist + any pre-warm requirements we should budget into the rollout? Also include any procurement lead times that would affect go-live by mid-Jan.

Thanks,
Rajiv
VP Product, Helion Labs
--
Helion Labs | ops@helionlabs.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Suresh <rajiv@helionlabs.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Helion — Dedicated pool: region & surge questions

Rajiv — thanks for the clear asks. High level answers up front, then an operational checklist attached (HL-dedicated-MAP-v1.xlsx).

1) Recommended primary region: europe-west3 (Amsterdam) as the EU-local option to meet residency / latency; configure us-west1 as secondary for dev/demo bursts routed with policy-based fallback.

2) Autoscale / burst approach:
- Baseline pool sized for steady-state (180 concurrent sessions) + 30% buffer.
- Burst lane (reserved warm nodes) sized to cover ~500 concurrent sessions with <100 ms cold-start risk.
- Dynamic fill to reach 1,400 uses cold-start parallelism + warm-step provisioning; to meet 2s median token latency we must pre-warm KV cache and keep a small warm standby of model variants.
- Fallback policy: route to quantized smaller variant (e.g., 7B int8) for non-critical routes and return 503 + retry hints for high-cost routes.

Operational checklist (attached) includes: procurement lead times, required NetOps entries, pre-warm script, pre-deploy traffic simulation, and SLA guardrails. Key procurement notes: regional node quotas in europe-west3 typically need 4–6 weeks reservation lead time for dedicated pools depending on capacity; we can leverage burst credits to shorten by ~2 weeks with a committed start date.

Action items:
- Rajiv: confirm EU data residency as strict (yes/no).
- Marta: share the demo cadence (dates) so we can pre-schedule warm lanes for those days.
- Monica/Karthik: draft the surge policy table for Helion (thresholds / pre-warm rules / model fallback) by Mon, Nov 23.

I attached the MAP workbook with an initial surge matrix and decision checkpoints. We'll iterate.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rajiv Suresh <rajiv@helionlabs.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Helion — Dedicated pool: region & surge questions

All — quick technical notes from infra that will affect the surge policy design:

- KV cache warmup: for your quantized 8-bit models, warmup time to fill KV cache for a single production model at current prompt profiles is ~18–26s per worker if cold. To meet 2s median at spike start we need a warm pool (standby workers) sized to cover first 30–60s of traffic.
- Autoscale granularity: we recommend a 15s control loop with continuous batching; hard policy is "warm standby" + "on-demand fill" rather than pure reactive provisioning.
- Routing rules: primary region should be eu-west3 with affinity; set a per-route SLO that allows fallback to smaller variant only for non-authenticated, non-financial routes.
- Pre-warm script: we will provide a script that primes KV caches using a representative trace (needs a 2-hour run in staging).
- Networking: netops entries for peering + AS path prep often take 7–10 business days. Add that to the lead time.

I'll push a draft surge-matrix and recommended worker counts into the MAP workbook by EOD Monday.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rajiv Suresh <rajiv@helionlabs.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marta Alvarez <marta@helionlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Helion — Dedicated pool: region & surge questions

Thanks — that helps a lot. A couple clarifications:

1) EU residency is strict for EU customers (yes). We can accept US fallback for internal dev demos only.
2) Demo cadence: weekly product webinars on Tue for the next 8 weeks with intermittent investor demo days where spikes hit ~1,200–1,400 concurrent sessions for 10–20 minutes.
3) Procurement timeline: we were hoping to sign by Dec 3 to meet a Jan 15 go-live. If europe-west3 lead time is 4–6 weeks, Dec 3 may be tight — can you confirm whether burst credits + pre-reserved warm standby is enough to meet Jan 15?

Marta will coordinate procurement with our legal and finance.

—Rajiv

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Suresh <rajiv@helionlabs.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marta Alvarez <marta@helionlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Helion — Dedicated pool: region & surge questions

Rajiv / Marta — quick agreement summary and next steps so procurement has a checklist: 

Agreed decisions:
- Primary region: europe-west3 (Amsterdam) for EU residency.
- Secondary region for dev/demos: us-west1 (route-only, no EU customer data).
- Surge approach: warm-standby lane sized to handle first 30–60s (approx 500 concurrent sessions), dynamic fill to cover additional bursts to 1,400 with quantized smaller-variant fallback for non-sensitive routes.
- Pre-warm requirement: 2-hour staged priming run + scheduled warm lanes for known demo dates.
- Procurement: target signature by Dec 3. We'll provision reserved warm standby for Jan 15 using burst credits to meet the launch if legal signs by Dec 3; NetOps lead time (7–10 business days) still applies.

Immediate next steps (owners & ETA):
- Marta (Helion): complete PO + legal approval by Dec 3.
- Monica: finalize SOW language for warm-standby + burst credits by Nov 27.
- Karthik: provide final surge-matrix and worker counts by Nov 25 (will update MAP workbook).
- Sean: create runbook for pre-warm script and schedule a 2-hour priming run in staging for Dec 7 (invite to follow).

I've attached the updated surge matrix PDF (surge-matrix-helion.pdf) and the MAP workbook. If any of the above needs different wording for contract language, flag it in the SOW draft and I'll loop legal.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the kickoff.

—Sean
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
